questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.question:
Consider the following two problems on undirected graphs:

  • $\alpha$: Given $G(V, E)$, does $G$ have an independent set of size |V| - $4$?
  • $\beta$: Given $G(V, E)$, does $G$ have an independent set of size $5$?

Which one of the following is TRUE?

Which one of the following is TRUE?

  1. $\alpha$ is in P and $\beta$ is NP-complete

  2. $\alpha$ is NP-complete and $\beta$ is in P

questions.title: GATE EC 2019 | GA Question: 4
questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.question:
Consider the following code written in a pass-by-reference language like FORTRAN and these statements about the code. 

subroutine swap(ix,iy) 
     it = ix 
L1 : ix = iy 
L2 : iy = it 
    end 
    ia = 3 
    ib = 8 
    call swap (ia, ib+5)
    print *, ia, ib 
    end

S1: The compiler will generate code to allocate a temporary nameless cell, initialize it to 13, and pass the address of the cell to swap 
S2: On execution the code will generate a runtime error on line L1 
S3: On execution the code will generate a runtime error on line L2 
S4: The program will print 13 and 8 
S5: The program will print 13 and -2 

Exactly the following set of statement(s) is correct:

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.question:
Consider this C code to swap two integers and these five statements: the code

  void swap (int *px, int *py) 
     { 
        *px = *px - *py;
        *py = *px + *py;
        *px = *py - *px;
     }

S1: will generate a compilation error 

S2: may generate a segmentation fault at runtime depending on the arguments passed 

S3: correctly implements the swap procedure for all input pointers referring to integers stored in memory locations accessible to the process

S4: implements the swap procedure correctly for some but not all valid input pointers 

S5: may add or subtract integers and pointers

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.question:
Consider the table employee(empId, name, department, salary) and the two queries $Q_1, \, Q_2$ below. Assuming that department $5$ has more than one employee, and we want to find the employees who get higher salary than anyone in the department $5,$ which one of the statements is TRUE for any arbitrary employee table?

$Q_1:$ 
Select e.empId
From employee e
Where not exists
    (Select * From employee s Where s.department = "5" and s.salary >= e.salary)
$Q_2:$ 
Select e.empId
From employee e
Where e.salary > Any
    (Select distinct salary From employee s Where s.department = "5")

questions.title: GATE EC 2019 | EC Question: 1
questions.subject: Control Systems
questions.question: The steady-state error $e_{ss}$ of a Type-1 unity feedback control system to a unit ramp input $r(t) = t \cdot u(t)$ is given by:
questions.explanation:
Step-by-Step Solution (Control Systems):

For a Type-1 system with unit ramp input: velocity error constant $K_v = \lim_{s \to 0} s G(s)$, and steady-state error $e_{ss} = \frac{1}{K_v}$.

questions.title: GATE EC 2019 | EC Question: 4
questions.subject: Electromagnetics & Antennas
questions.question: A lossless transmission line with characteristic impedance $Z_0 = 50\,\Omega$ is terminated in a load impedance $Z_L = 100\,\Omega$. The voltage reflection coefficient $\Gamma$ is:
questions.explanation:
Step-by-Step Solution (Electromagnetics & Antennas):

$\Gamma = \frac{Z_L - Z_0}{Z_L + Z_0} = \frac{100 - 50}{100 + 50} = \frac{50}{150} = +\frac{1}{3} = +0.333$.

questions.title: GATE EC 2019 | EC Question: 26
questions.subject: Network Theory
questions.question: A linear bilateral DC network has an open-circuit voltage $V_{\text{th}} = 30\text{ V}$ and short-circuit current $I_{\text{sc}} = 5\text{ A}$ across terminals A and B. The Thevenin equivalent resistance $R_{\text{th}}$ (in Ohms) is ________.
questions.explanation:
Step-by-Step Solution (Network Theory):

$R_{\text{th}} = \frac{V_{\text{th}}}{I_{\text{sc}}} = \frac{30\text{ V}}{5\text{ A}} = 6.0\,\Omega$.

questions.title: GATE EC 2019 | EC Question: 31
questions.subject: Electronic Devices (EDC)
questions.question: An abrupt Silicon $p\text{-}n$ junction has built-in potential $V_{bi} = 0.8\text{ V}$. The transition capacitance at zero bias is $C_{j0} = 20\text{ pF}$. When reverse biased with $V_R = 3.2\text{ V}$, the junction capacitance $C_j = \frac{C_{j0}}{\sqrt{1 + V_R / V_{bi}}}$ (in $\text{pF}$) is ________.
questions.explanation:
Step-by-Step Solution (Electronic Devices (EDC)):

$C_j = \frac{20}{\sqrt{1 + 3.2/0.8}} = \frac{20}{\sqrt{1 + 4}} = \frac{20}{\sqrt{5}} = \frac{20}{2.236} \approx 8.94\text{ pF}$.

questions.question: A non-inverting operational amplifier circuit has $R_1 = 5\,\text{k}\Omega$ connected from the inverting pin to ground and feedback resistor $R_f = 45\,\text{k}\Omega$. The closed-loop voltage gain $A_v = 1 + \frac{R_f}{R_1}$ is ________.

Step-by-Step Solution (Analog Circuits):

$A_v = 1 + \frac{R_f}{R_1} = 1 + \frac{45}{5} = 1 + 9 = 10.0$.

questions.title: GATE EC 2019 | EC Question: 46
questions.subject: Digital Circuits
questions.question: A mod-16 ripple counter is built using 4 toggle ($T$) flip-flops. If the input clock frequency is $32\text{ kHz}$, the output frequency (in $\text{kHz}$) at the final flip-flop is ________.
questions.explanation:
Step-by-Step Solution (Digital Circuits):

A counter with $N = 4$ flip-flops has modulus $2^N = 16$. Each flip-flop divides frequency by 2: $f_{\text{out}} = \frac{f_{\text{in}}}{16} = \frac{32\text{ kHz}}{16} = 2\text{ kHz}$.

questions.title: GATE EC 2019 | EC Question: 54
questions.subject: Communications & Information Theory
questions.question: An AM broadcast signal has a carrier power $P_c = 10\text{ kW}$ and modulation index $\mu = 0.8$. The total transmitted power $P_t = P_c \left(1 + \frac{\mu^2}{2}\right)$ (in $\text{kW}$) is ________.
questions.explanation:
Step-by-Step Solution (Communications & Information Theory):

$P_t = 10 \left(1 + \frac{0.8^2}{2}\right) = 10 \left(1 + \frac{0.64}{2}\right) = 10(1 + 0.32) = 13.2\text{ kW}$.

questions.title: GATE EC 2019 | EC Question: 55
questions.subject: Communications & Information Theory
questions.question: According to Shannon's Channel Capacity theorem, the capacity $C$ of an additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) channel with bandwidth $B$ and signal-to-noise ratio $\text{SNR} = S/N$ is:
questions.explanation:
Step-by-Step Solution (Communications & Information Theory):

Shannon-Hartley theorem states maximum error-free transmission capacity is $C = B \log_2 (1 + \text{SNR})$ bits/second.
